text:
The Golden Knights went into Edmonton on Tuesday as the team chasing, and left with a 5-3 win and a sense that the Pacific Division may run through Las Vegas again. They're 15-6-5 under first-year coach Ryan Craig, who was promoted from AHL Henderson in June after Vegas lost the Stanley Cup Final to Carolina in six games.

The underlying numbers are the best part. Vegas takes 55% of the expected goals, and it has actually scored about four fewer goals than its chances deserve. That's the opposite of the Oilers' story, and it's why our numbers give Vegas a 59% chance to win the division and a projected 106 points.

The faces of it: Mark Stone became the franchise's career points leader last week, Jack Eichel scored twice in Edmonton, and rookie Trevor Connelly had his first three-point night, which The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted puts him atop the rookie scoring race. Victor Olofsson has 10 points in his last ten games, though on 6.8 expected. The Stone, Ivan Barbashev and Eichel line wins its minutes comfortably (59% of expected goals), and Brayden McNabb with Shea Theodore anchors the back end.

The worry spots are on the margins: the Nic Dowd line (37%) and the Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon pair (42%) give back chances. Craig said in camp he'd play both goalies, and Adin Hill has been good lately (3.8 goals saved above expected over five starts). The depth minutes are what to watch.
headline: Vegas is better than its record says
